subject: Interop runbook + co-engineering checklist for LangChain / LlamaIndex adapters
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex@signalforge.io>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: interop runbook + tracehook approach for LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters

Hi Aisha,

Quick intro — I’m Alex (Product) at SignalForge. We’re working on a managed vector-search product and want to ship a Redwood-backed runtime option for our customers. Several prospects use LangChain/LLamaIndex client stacks and ask about runtime tracing and adapter compatibility.

Two asks:
1) Do you have a co-engineering "interop runbook" that summarizes best-practice checks (streaming, function-calls, kv-cache, tokenization/quantization gotchas) when validating adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex?
2) What tracing hooks do you expose (correlation ids, span naming, per-token telemetry)? We want to ensure traces can link from client SDKs -> Redwood runtime -> model variant.

Attached a short outline of our expectations (proposal_outline.pdf). Can we set up a 30-minute sync next week?

Thanks,
Alex Park
Product Partnerships | SignalForge

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex@signalforge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: interop runbook + tracehook approach for LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the outline. Looping in Marissa (partnerships) and Jonas (integrations engineering) so we can produce a focused runbook and answer the tracing specifics.

High level: we do maintain an internal checklist for ISV adapters; it covers protocol binding (sync/async), streaming compatibility, chunking/tokenization mismatches, KV cache semantics, model variant fallbacks, and instrumentation expectations. I’m attaching a short questionnaire (interop-questionnaire.csv) with the fields we typically use during a technical eval — can you fill the sections on your client-side SDK behavior (how you batch requests, default streaming vs polling, use of function-calls)?

Jonas — can you review the tracing bullet below and confirm the minimal span set we should require from an adapter: request.start, request.model_resolve, token.generate (optional per-token), request.finish. We recommend propagating: request_id (UUID), user_request_id (optional), and model_variant. Also we surface a trace link header (X-Redwood-Trace) so partners can stitch traces server-side.

Proposed next steps:
- Alex/Tina: complete questionnaire by EOD Tue (2027-05-25)
- Internal: Jonas to draft one-page trace requirements; Marissa to map contractual SOW language (credits/priority support)
- Schedule 30-min sync Wed or Thu next week to review runbook draft

Happy to own consolidation once we have the questionnaire back.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Partner Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T10:33:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: SF runbook scope + task split

Thanks for looping me in — quick internal plan so we can move fast: 

1) Scope (Jonas lead): technical checklist that covers
   - Client bindings: sync vs async, websocket vs SSE streaming semantics
   - Tokenization & vocabulary alignment: confirm tokenizer + pre/post-processing steps
   - KV cache behavior: expected cache warmup, eviction policy, and how to validate cache hits in integration tests
   - Quantization effects: expected numeric divergence at 8-bit/4-bit and recommended eval prompts
   - Function/tool calls: JSON schema conformance, response length/cutoff handling

2) Observability & tracing (Vivek + Jonas):
   - Minimal span model (start/model_resolve/token_finish/request_finish) and required tags
   - Correlation: request_id, adapter_request_id, model_variant, region
   - Export formats: OTLP/HTTP and simple trace header for partners to include in client SDKs

3) Partner-facing runbook (Aisha + Marissa):
   - One-page checklist + 3 example curl flows (streaming, function-call, embed)
   - Test harness instructions (unit/e2e + synthetic latency) and pass/fail criteria
   - Legal/finance bullets we may ask for in the SOW (support hours, priority queuing)

Deliverables & owners:
- Jonas: runbook technical appendix draft (due 2027-05-24)
- Vivek: trace spec + sample_trace_config.yaml (due 2027-05-24)
- Aisha/Marissa: consolidated partner runbook draft and HubSpot attachment (due 2027-05-26)

Note: HubSpot deal SF-2027-0421 is open; I’ll add the draft as an attachment and propose the 30-min slot once we have the questionnaire filled.

Marissa
Head of ISV Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex@signalforge.io>, Tina Morales <tina@peppertech.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-26T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Interop runbook draft + next steps (LangChain / LlamaIndex)

Alex / Tina — thanks for the patience. We consolidated a short runbook and a technical appendix for your integration team. Key items included:

- Checklist summary (one page): streaming behavior, function-call schema, tokenizer alignment, KV-cache validation, quantization guidance.
- Trace spec: minimal spans + required tags (request_id, adapter_request_id, model_variant), and the X-Redwood-Trace HTTP header to stitch traces.
- Test harness: repo + simple scripts (three curl examples) and synthetic latency tests to verify fallbacks and batching.
- Known gotchas: token truncation differences between our runtime and some LangChain tokenizers; suggested pre-tokenization step included.

Attached: runbook_draft.pdf, sample_trace_config.yaml. Also shared a Google Drive draft here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1XcRunbookDraft
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345/SF-2027-0421

Next steps I propose:
1) Alex/Tina — confirm you received the attachments and whether you prefer a walkthrough demo Tue (2027-05-31) or Thu (2027-06-02)
2) Fill the questionnaire if you haven’t already; the answers let Jonas scope a short adapter test-suite doc
3) We’ll include a 4-hour zero-cost co-engineering window in the SOW for the first integration milestone (Marissa will draft SOW language)

If that works, I’ll lock a calendar invite for the demo and drop the runbook into the HubSpot attachment area.

Cheers,
Aisha Rahman
Partner Solutions | Redwood Inference
